title: General Biology I & II
description: Builds an integrated year-long foundation in cellular, molecular, genetic, evolutionary, organismal, ecological, and field-based biology, with enough data literacy and scientific reasoning to prepare students for environmental science and later biology coursework.

topics.title: Biology as Evidence-Based Science
topics.description: This opening topic teaches biology as a way of asking questions, designing tests, interpreting evidence, and reasoning across scales.

children.title: Scientific inquiry
children.description: Students learn how biological knowledge is built from testable explanations and carefully designed observations.

children.title: Biological data literacy
children.description: Students practice reading graphs, interpreting variation, and making claims from data.

children.title: Levels of biological organization
children.description: A scale map helps students connect molecules, cells, organisms, populations, communities, and ecosystems.

topics.title: Chemistry of Life and Biological Molecules
topics.description: Living systems are chemical systems. This topic explains how water, carbon, weak interactions, and macromolecules make life possible.

children.title: Water, pH, and weak interactions
children.description: Students learn why water chemistry shapes structure, reactions, and transport in organisms.

children.title: Carbon chemistry
children.description: Carbon's bonding patterns explain the diversity of biological molecules.

children.title: Macromolecules
children.description: Students connect molecular structure to biological function.

topics.title: Cell Structure and Function
topics.description: Cells are the basic units of life, and their internal organization explains how living systems maintain order and perform work.

children.title: Cell theory and microscopy
children.description: Students learn why cells are central to biology and how cell structures are observed.

children.title: Cell types and organelles
children.description: Comparing prokaryotes and eukaryotes clarifies shared features and specialized compartments.

children.title: Cytoskeleton and cellular organization
children.description: The cytoskeleton gives cells shape, movement, transport, and mechanical organization.

topics.title: Membranes, Transport, and Cell Communication
topics.description: Membranes regulate exchange and communication, letting cells maintain homeostasis and coordinate responses.

children.title: Membrane structure
children.description: Students learn how phospholipids and proteins create selective, dynamic boundaries.

children.title: Transport mechanisms
children.description: Transport explains how substances cross membranes with or against gradients.

children.title: Cell signaling
children.description: Students see how cells detect signals and convert them into molecular and behavioral responses.

topics.title: Energy, Enzymes, and Metabolism
topics.description: This topic explains how cells transform matter and energy through controlled chemical pathways.

children.title: Bioenergetics
children.description: Students learn how free energy, ATP, and redox chemistry drive cellular work.

children.title: Enzymes
children.description: Enzymes make biological reactions fast and regulated.

children.title: Metabolic networks
children.description: Students learn pathways as integrated systems rather than isolated reactions.

topics.title: Cellular Respiration and Photosynthesis
topics.description: Respiration and photosynthesis are the core energy transformations that link cells to ecosystems and global cycles.

children.title: Cellular respiration
children.description: Students learn how cells harvest energy from organic molecules.

children.title: Photosynthesis
children.description: Students learn how light energy becomes chemical energy and fixed carbon.

children.title: Energy flow in ecosystems
children.description: This connects cellular energetics to food webs and productivity.

topics.title: Cell Cycle, Mitosis, and Meiosis
topics.description: Cell division explains growth, repair, reproduction, and the movement of genetic information across generations.

children.title: Cell cycle regulation
children.description: Students learn how cells coordinate growth, DNA replication, and division.

children.title: G1, S, G2, and M Phases
Mitosis
children.description: Mitosis explains how genetically identical daughter cells form.

children.title: Meiosis
children.description: Meiosis explains gamete formation and genetic variation.

topics.title: DNA, Gene Expression, and Molecular Genetics
topics.description: This topic connects DNA structure to replication, gene expression, mutation, and biotechnology.

children.title: DNA replication and genome organization
children.description: Students learn how genetic information is copied and packaged.

children.title: Transcription and translation
children.description: Students learn how genetic information becomes RNA and protein.

children.title: Mutation and biotechnology
children.description: Students connect genetic variation to modern tools and ethical questions.

topics.title: Genetics and Inheritance
topics.description: Genetics gives students a quantitative language for predicting inheritance and connecting genes to traits.

children.title: Mendelian inheritance
children.description: Students learn segregation, independent assortment, and probability-based genetic prediction.

children.title: Chromosomal inheritance
children.description: Chromosomes explain linkage, sex-linked traits, and recombination.

children.title: Population and quantitative genetics preview
children.description: This bridges genetics to evolution and complex traits.

topics.title: Evolutionary Mechanisms
topics.description: Evolution is the unifying framework of biology, explaining both unity and diversity across life.

children.title: Sources of variation
children.description: Students learn how heritable variation enters populations.

children.title: Mechanisms of evolution
children.description: Students learn the processes that change allele frequencies over time.

children.title: Evidence for evolution
children.description: Students connect evolutionary theory to data from fossils, molecules, anatomy, and biogeography.

topics.title: Speciation, Phylogeny, and the History of Life
topics.description: This topic helps students reason about biological diversity through common ancestry and branching evolutionary history.

children.title: Speciation
children.description: Students learn how populations become reproductively isolated and form new species.

children.title: Phylogenetic thinking
children.description: Tree thinking helps students interpret relationships among organisms.

children.title: Origins and major transitions
children.description: Students connect Earth's history to the evolution of life.

topics.title: Biodiversity: Prokaryotes, Protists, Fungi, Plants, and Animals
topics.description: A combined biology sequence should introduce the major branches of life and the traits that make them ecologically and evolutionarily important.

children.title: Microbial diversity
children.description: Students learn that bacteria, archaea, protists, and fungi are central to ecosystems and evolution.

children.title: Plant diversity
children.description: Students learn how plants diversified onto land and transformed ecosystems.

children.title: Animal diversity
children.description: Students learn major animal body plans and evolutionary innovations.

topics.title: Plant Structure and Physiology
topics.description: Plant physiology connects anatomy, transport, photosynthesis, reproduction, and environmental response.

children.title: Plant tissues and organs
children.description: Students learn how roots, stems, leaves, and vascular tissues support plant function.

children.title: Plant transport and regulation
children.description: Students learn how water, sugar, and signals move through plants.

children.title: Plant reproduction and responses
children.description: This links life cycles to environmental cues and adaptation.

topics.title: Animal Physiology Overview
topics.description: Animal physiology shows how body systems maintain homeostasis, exchange materials, and respond to environments.

children.title: Homeostasis
children.description: Students learn how animals regulate internal conditions.

children.title: Exchange and transport systems
children.description: Students compare how animals move gases, nutrients, wastes, and signals.

children.title: Control and coordination
children.description: Nervous and endocrine systems show how animals sense and respond.

topics.title: Population and Community Ecology
topics.description: Ecology begins with organisms interacting with each other and their environments across space and time.

children.title: Population ecology
children.description: Students learn how population size changes and what limits growth.

children.title: Species interactions
children.description: Interactions explain community structure and evolutionary pressure.

children.title: Community structure
children.description: Students learn how diversity, disturbance, and succession shape communities.

topics.title: Ecosystem Processes and Conservation Biology
topics.description: This topic links energy flow, nutrient cycling, biodiversity, and human impacts into environmental decision-making.

children.title: Ecosystem ecology
children.description: Students learn how energy and matter move through ecosystems.

children.title: Biodiversity and conservation
children.description: Students learn why biodiversity matters and how it is threatened.

children.title: Climate and human impacts
children.description: Students connect biological systems to environmental change and stewardship.

topics.title: Biological Field, Lab, and Data Methods
topics.description: A combined sequence should end with students able to collect, interpret, and communicate biological evidence.

children.title: Lab and field methods
children.description: Students learn basic techniques used to study cells, genes, organisms, and ecosystems.

children.title: Data quality and analysis
children.description: Students learn that biological conclusions depend on careful measurement and uncertainty handling.

children.title: Research communication
children.description: Students practice turning observations and data into clear scientific arguments.
